chunks: Mūsā ibn Bakr narrated from Zurārah, who said:
I heard Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام saying:
The waiting period of mutʿah is forty-five days.
It is as though I am looking at Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام counting forty-five days with his hand.
Then when the term comes, the separation takes place without divorce.

key_terms.الْأَجَلُ: the appointed term or fixed duration of the marriage contract
key_terms.خَمْسَةٌ وَ أَرْبَعُونَ يَوْمًا: the legally specified duration of forty-five days
key_terms.عِدَّةُ: the waiting period a woman must observe after the end of a marriage

ai.seo_question: What is the ʿiddah of mutʿah, and does its end require divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the ʿiddah of mutʿah, stating that it is forty-five days. It also clarifies that when the specified term of the temporary marriage ends, separation occurs automatically and does not require ṭalāq.
